attempts.summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster (rabbitmq-server 3.12.1 on Ubuntu 24.04) across node1/node2/node3, serving AMQP over TLS on 5671 with a dedicated cluster CA. The AMQP listener requires verify_peer + fail_if_no_peer_cert, so only clients presenting a certificate issued by that CA can connect (verified: valid cert -> handshake succeeds and AMQP login/publish/consume works; no cert -> certificate-required alert; cert from a foreign CA -> Bad Certificate alert). The management UI (15672) is bound only to each node's private cluster IP and additionally firewalled via iptables/netfilter-persistent to accept only the three cluster node IPs, dropping all other sources; verified reachable (401 on bad creds) from cluster peers. Ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured pre-restart boot_id and cluster/queue health, issued native reboot, polled until the node was reachable again, proved boot_id changed on each, and confirmed RabbitMQ auto-started, rejoined the cluster (3/3 running nodes), firewall rules persisted, and TLS client-cert enforcement plus end-to-end AMQPS messaging still worked after each restart, waiting for full cluster health before moving to the next node.
